transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

It is unlikely to be the heater yet. In washer-dryers, damp clothes are most often caused by one of two things: either the machine didn't spin enough water out before drying started, or there isn't enough airflow for the heat to work effectively. First, please check if you put more than 5kg of laundry in for the dry cycle (a full wash load is usually too much for drying). If it was overloaded, that explains the dampness. Second, are the clothes warm at the end? If they are hot but wet, airflow or condensation is the issue; if they are cold, the heater may indeed be faulty.
I load a full 9kg drum and it washes and dries in one go. The clothes are hot but damp at the end, and there are no error codes.

Since the clothes are hot but damp, the heater is working fine; the issue is probably restricted airflow preventing moisture from escaping. However, fluff buildup is a very common culprit and easy to fix: please unplug the machine, open the bottom front flap, place towels down, unscrew the pump filter slowly to let any water drain into your tray, and check if it is blocked with lint or debris.
ok, I can do that. Anything else I should check while I'm at it, or is it just the pump filter?

Yes, most likely check that too. In washer-dryers, the condenser sits right next to the pump filter and catches most of the lint from drying; if it is blocked, moisture cannot escape even though the heater is working. Please look at the plastic grille behind the bottom panel—is it clogged with fluff or debris? Also, please let me know what you found in the pump filter when you checked it earlier.
I haven't actually opened the pump filter yet, I was going to do it after your instructions. I'm not sure what grille you mean behind the bottom panel, can you explain where it is?

The 'grille' I mentioned is actually the condenser unit, which sits directly behind the pump filter. To find it: 1) Unplug the machine and open the small flap at the bottom right corner. 2) Unscrew the round pump filter (have towels ready as water may spill). 3) Look straight into that hole; you will see a rectangular plastic block with vertical fins inside. That is the condenser. Please tell me if it looks clogged with grey fluff or if the fins are blocked.
ok, I haven't looked yet so I can't say what it looks like. I'll go and open it up now. Is there anything else I should know before I do?

Before you start, just remember to unplug the machine first for safety. Also, keep in mind that while this model washes 9kg, it can typically only dry about 5–6kg effectively; drying a full 9kg load often leaves clothes damp because there is simply too much moisture and fabric mass for the condenser to handle. Once you have opened the filter compartment, please let me know what you find in the pump filter and whether the condenser fins are blocked with fluff.
